skills.name: Numbers, figures, words and currency names

note.text: Figures represent numbers with numerals; words express the same number in language. Read place value and zeros carefully, then preserve the currency unit. An amount in CFA francs is not automatically the same purchasing value as the same numeral in another currency. This lesson names currencies but supplies no exchange-rate exercise or payment instruction. Number-word conventions can vary; the model follows the written model shown here and the teacher should confirm accepted examination styles.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to match a number phrase to its figure and name the currencies in a checked country list. Builds on: word meaning, written forms and place-value knowledge. Leads to: a written money script and precise quantities in reports.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original model amount: {12500} CFA francs is {words(12500)} CFA francs. Country examples: Cameroon uses the Central African CFA franc, XAF; Nigeria the naira, NGN; Ghana the Ghana cedi, GHS; the United Kingdom pound sterling, GBP. Codes help distinguish currencies with similar names. These names do not imply that any two currencies can be interchanged without considering conversion.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Group digits by place value, read the full phrase and check the unit. When speaking is practised later, a teacher should check how the amount is pronounced; this screen checks written recognition. Do not infer a current exchange rate from a country/currency list.

the value determined by a digit’s position

cards.idea: Distinguish the ideas used in this lesson.
example: number words: a linguistic written representation of a number.
place value: the value determined by a digit’s position.
currency label: the unit identifying which money an amount refers to.

cards.idea: Read the whole example before identifying its function.
example: The model writes an amount using numerals.
The phrase {words(12500)} represents the model amount.
The learner checks zeros before accepting an amount.
The amount names CFA francs instead of leaving the unit unknown.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve the intended meaning and form.
example: Figures means a person’s bank signature. Correction: Figures represent a number rather than identifying a signatory.
Words and figures may disagree without changing the amount. Correction: Both representations should express the same value.
An added zero never changes a number’s value. Correction: A zero can change the place values of the other digits.
Identical numerals in every currency necessarily buy the same amount. Correction: Currency identity and value cannot be inferred from the numeral alone.
